card.title: The Trusted Deputy
card.instruction: Act as the reliable second-in-command, managing access and details while quietly shaping every decision.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The captain's finishing her briefing. As first mate, I'm collecting harbor updates.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: North harbor's closed. South and west both have berths available.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll flag the closure immediately and attach my recommendation for west.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll report the options myself. I haven't recommended either.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. I'll introduce you and bring both berth sheets. West's booking form is already filled in; I'll leave it beside her pen.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's harbor options inform A3's recommendation; B4's direct-report plan leads A5 to preserve influence through document placement.

relationship.evidence: B2 supplies operational information and B4 insists on presenting both options without endorsing one.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's direct access, but the already-completed west form is a late convenience rather than a newly enacted steering choice.
